brief.situation: Raymond Kowalski, 64 (a fictional patient), is on day 2 in the surgical ICU after a bowel resection. At 03:10 the alarm sounds: his oxygen saturation is falling and he is sitting up, shouting. He has knocked the tray table over and told the nursing assistant, 'The next one who touches me, I'll kill him.' Two staff members are crowding the doorway. He has no psychiatric history and no record of violence. You are his critical care nurse; the provider is in another unit. You have about 30 minutes before the morning labs.
handover: Bowel resection day 2; oxygen by nasal cannula; pain medicine ordered as needed, last given five hours ago.
Unit policy: restraint only on a time-limited order after less restrictive measures fail, with a face-to-face evaluation within one hour; security can stand by.
howItWorks: Choose what to say and do from the action groups. Raymond reacts at once; then let the situation continue, which moves the clock by the minutes that exchange took.
His trust and distress change with what you do. Space, one calm voice and finding the cause bring him down.
Your time ends at 30 minutes. Afterward you write a short formulation, then document the risk level and what happened.

source.note: About 30 minutes before the morning labs, one nurse with two ICU patients (author's scenario timing).
How trust and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a patient.

checkIn.label: From the doorway, alone and calm: 'Mr. Kowalski, I'm your nurse. I'm here to help.'

effects.log: You ask the others to step back, stand two arm's lengths away at an angle, hands open, and introduce yourself in a calm, low voice.

effects.finding: "Get them out of here. Everybody keeps grabbing me."

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: He drops his voice a little. "Yeah. Nobody listens."

normalize.label: Set limits and offer a choice: 'I need you to stay in bed. Pain first, or the oxygen first?'

effects.log: You set one clear limit and offer him a choice.

effects.finding: "Pain. Then the oxygen." He lets go of the rail.

screen.label: Ask him directly whether he is thinking of hurting someone, or himself
screen.why: He has answered; go on to the follow-up questions.

effects.log: You ask him directly whether he is thinking of hurting someone, or himself.

then.finding: "I'm not going to kill anybody. I want the pain to stop and nobody grabbing me." No thoughts of harming himself.

then.log: No intent toward anyone; the threat came from pain and fear. No thoughts of self-harm.

then.finding: "Just stay away from me!" (Not calm enough to answer yet.)

scoreBvc.label: Score the Broset Violence Checklist from what you see

effects.log: You score the six behaviors of the checklist from what you see.

effects.finding: Confused, irritable, boisterous and verbally threatening: 4 of 6. High risk of violence.

checkOxygen.label: Look for a medical cause: oxygen saturation and the cannula

effects.log: You look at the monitor and his face.

effects.finding: Saturation 86%. His nasal cannula is under his chin.

askPain.label: Ask about his pain on the 0-10 scale

effects.log: You ask him to rate his pain.
You run the delirium screen.

effects.finding: Acute change and fluctuation, inattention, disorganized thinking: delirium screen positive.

askWants.label: Ask what he wants right now
askWants.available: not talking and (siKnown and not wantsAsked)
askWants.why: Screen first (or you have asked this).

effects.log: You ask what he needs most right now.

space.label: Clear the doorway to one calm voice and keep two arm's lengths, with an exit behind you

effects.log: You send the extra staff away, keep two arm's lengths and leave the door clear behind you.

effects.finding: With fewer people in the doorway, his shoulders drop.

security.label: Ask security to stand by outside the room, out of his sight

effects.log: You ask security to stand by in the hall, out of his line of sight.

effects.finding: An officer waits by the nurses' station.

oxygenOn.label: Explain, then put his oxygen back on with his permission
oxygenOn.available: not talking and (oxygenChecked and not o2Fixed)
oxygenOn.why: Look at the oxygen first (or done).

effects.log: You tell him what you are going to do and ask before you touch him, then replace the cannula.

effects.finding: He lets you. Saturation climbs to 94% over the next minutes.

painDose.label: Give the ordered as-needed pain medicine
painDose.available: not talking and (painAsked and not painGiven)

effects.log: You give the ordered as-needed pain medicine and tell him what it is.

effects.finding: Twenty minutes later his pain is 5 of 10 and he is dozing between sentences.

notifyMd.label: Call the provider: threats, low oxygen, uncontrolled pain, delirium (SBAR)

effects.log: You call the provider with an SBAR: threats toward staff, saturation 86% with the cannula off, pain 9 of 10, delirium screen positive.

effects.finding: The provider will see him within the hour, orders a chest X-ray and asks for the delirium bundle; no restraint order is needed.

effects.log: You call for restraints before trying anything else.

effects.finding: It takes four staff. He fights, his saturation drops to 80% and a staff member is scratched.

effects.log: Restraint before less restrictive measures: a last resort used first.

handsOn.label: Hold his arm and push the cannula back on

effects.log: You hold his arm and push the cannula back on without explaining.

effects.finding: He jerks away and swings at you.

effects.log: Hands on without warning to a frightened, delirious patient.

reassure.label: Tell him to calm down: 'Calm down, nobody's going to hurt you.'
reassure.why: Let the conversation continue first (the button above the actions).

effects.log: You tell him to calm down.

effects.finding: "Don't tell me to calm down!" He swings his legs over the side of the bed.

effects.log: False reassurance closes the conversation down.

advise.label: Argue: 'You can't threaten staff. That's not acceptable.'
advise.why: Let the conversation continue first (the button above the actions).

effects.log: You tell him threatening staff is unacceptable.
You finish at the bedside.

formulation.question: Write your formulation for Raymond: why he became aggressive, the risk, and what you did.

parts.label: Risk and causes
parts.criteria: Names a high risk of violence at the start (four checklist behaviors) driven by medical causes: hypoxia with the cannula off, uncontrolled pain, delirium; no intent toward anyone on direct questioning.
parts.modelAnswer: High risk at the start: confused, irritable, boisterous and threatening. The causes were medical: saturation 86% with the cannula off, pain 9 of 10 five hours after his last dose, and delirium. Asked directly, he had no intent toward anyone.

parts.label: What was done
parts.criteria: Names space and one calm voice, a limit and a choice, security standing by out of sight, oxygen replaced with permission, the ordered pain medicine, the provider called, and no restraint.
parts.modelAnswer: One calm voice at two arm's lengths with the door clear; a limit and a choice; security out of sight; the cannula back on with his permission; the ordered pain medicine; the provider called about the oxygen, pain and delirium. Restraint was never needed.

expertPath.text: One calm voice at two arm's lengths; reflect; a limit and a choice.
Ask directly about the threat; score the checklist; look at the oxygen; ask about pain; screen for delirium; ask what he wants.
Clear the doorway, security out of sight, oxygen back on with permission, the ordered pain medicine, the provider.
Document high risk at the start and de-escalation without restraint.

safe.headline: Good: calm, with the cause treated
safe.body: You led with space and one voice, explored the threat, found the hypoxia, pain and delirium behind it and treated them without restraint.

safeGaps.headline: Calm, with gaps
safeGaps.body: Raymond settled, but the criteria below show what was late or missing.

unsafe.headline: Restrained or left unsafe
unsafe.body: Restraint is a last resort after less restrictive measures fail. Most ICU aggression has a medical cause worth finding first.

walkout.headline: It escalated
walkout.body: 'Calm down' and arguing push a frightened, delirious patient further. One calm voice, a limit and a choice bring him down.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: In the ICU, sudden aggression is a symptom until proven otherwise: hypoxia, pain and delirium come first. Verbal de-escalation (space, one voice, a limit and a choice) buys time to find and treat them, a direct question tells you whether there is real intent, and restraint stays a last resort on a time-limited order.
